day_context.tournament_summary: The first semi-final, and a rematch nobody in blue has forgotten. Two summers ago, at Euro 2024, Spain knocked France out at the semi-final stage — a 16-year-old named Lamine Yamal curling in from distance on the way to the trophy — and France have been waiting to answer it ever since. Tonight they get the chance in the biggest room of all: AT&T Stadium in Dallas, ~94,000 seats, the largest venue at the tournament, and a World Cup semi-final on the line. The strange thing is that the ledger everyone actually shares points the other way. France and Spain have met only once at a World Cup — the 2006 Round of 16 — and France won it, Zidane scoring the last goal of his last tournament to send a young Spain home. So there are two rivalries here, and they disagree: the recent one, where Spain are the reigning European champions and beat France when it mattered; and the World Cup one, where Spain have never beaten France at all. One of them settles tonight, and the winner goes to the final at MetLife.
context_notes: France vs Spain at AT&T Stadium, Arlington/Dallas — the first of the two World Cup semi-finals; the winner reaches the July 19 final at MetLife.

This is a rematch of the Euro 2024 semi-final, which Spain won 2-1 in Munich (9 Jul 2024) on the way to the European title — France ahead early through Kolo Muani before Lamine Yamal, then 16, equalised with a long-range strike and Dani Olmo won it.

But France have never lost to Spain at a World Cup: their only previous meeting was the 2006 Round of 16, France winning 3-1 in Hanover with Zinedine Zidane scoring the final goal of his career-ending tournament.
France are the 2018 world champions and 2022 runners-up (beaten on penalties by Argentina); win tonight and they become only the third nation ever to reach three consecutive World Cup finals.

Spain, the reigning European champions and 2010 world champions, have reached the semi-final unbeaten — 0-0 Cape Verde, 4-0 Saudi Arabia, 1-0 Uruguay, then 3-0 Austria, 1-0 Portugal and 2-1 Belgium in the knockouts.
France lost 4-1 to Norway in the group stage and still arrived here, beating Sweden 3-0, Paraguay 1-0 and Morocco 2-0 in the knockout rounds.

here_there_thread.topic: The rivalry that can't agree with itself
here_there_thread.framing: France and Spain have spent forty years trading eras, and the record depends entirely on which competition you point at. Point at the World Cup and Spain have never beaten France — one meeting, 2006, France 3-1, Zidane's goodbye. Point at the European Championship and the ledger flips: Spain put France out at Euro 2012, and again at the Euro 2024 semi-final, where a 16-year-old called Lamine Yamal announced himself by curling a shot in from twenty-five yards and the reigning-champions-to-be went through 2-1. In between sits France's own revenge — the 2021 Nations League final in Milan, won 2-1 by a Mbappé goal Spain still insist was offside. It is a rivalry that keeps changing hands and never settling, because the two keep meeting in different tournaments and the winner is never the same twice. Tonight, for the first time, they meet in a World Cup semi-final in the United States — Spain the European champions carrying the most recent word, France the World Cup side that has never lost this fixture on this stage. Both of those things cannot survive the night.

story_behind_number.surface_stat: France in the semi-final, and the number is 3
story_behind_number.historical_anchor: Win tonight and France reach a third World Cup final in a row — 2018, 2022, 2026 — and only two nations in the history of the tournament have ever done that. West Germany did it across 1982, 1986 and 1990, losing the first two and winning the last. Brazil did it across 1994, 1998 and 2002, winning the first and third. Nobody else has managed three straight, not the great Hungary or Netherlands sides, not Italy, not anyone. France are one win from joining that two-team club: they beat Croatia to win 2018, lost the 2022 final to Argentina on penalties after Mbappé's hat-trick couldn't quite save them, and now stand ninety minutes from a third consecutive final. The number is a measure of a generation's grip on the sport — a France side that has been in the last act of the World Cup for eight straight years and is trying to make it twelve. Spain, standing in the way, would rather it stayed a two-team club.

narrative_beats: It is the only time France and Spain have ever met at a World Cup, and it doubled as a funeral for one idea and a coronation for another: 27 June 2006, Hanover, Spain young and rising, France old and — everyone had decided — finished.

Spain led. David Villa's penalty on 28 minutes fit the story everyone had written in advance: a fresh Spanish generation putting the veterans of France, Zidane and Vieira and Thuram and Makélélé, out to pasture. For an hour it held.

Then the old side refused the script. Franck Ribéry equalised before half-time, Patrick Vieira headed France ahead with seven minutes left, and in stoppage time Zinedine Zidane — playing the last tournament of his life, about to retire after the final — dribbled in the third. 3-1, and Spain went home.

Zidane would reach the 2006 final, score again from the penalty spot, headbutt Marco Materazzi, get sent off, and vanish from football with a red card. The goal in Hanover was the last he scored at a World Cup that did not end in the sport's most famous dismissal — and the last word, for twenty years, on France versus Spain.

back_story.ledger: France and Spain have met only once at a World Cup — the 2006 Round of 16, France 3-1 — and Spain have never beaten them on this stage. The wider rivalry is where Spain hold cards: they knocked France out of Euro 2012 and, more painfully, the Euro 2024 semi-final on the way to the European title, a 16-year-old Lamine Yamal scoring from distance. France's answer was the 2021 Nations League final, won 2-1 by a contested Mbappé goal. So the head-to-head everyone actually carries into tonight depends on the trophy: at the World Cup, France have never lost to Spain; at the Euros, Spain keep ending France's summers. One of those streaks breaks in Dallas.

video.title: France 3-1 Spain, 2006 — the veterans answer
video.caption: The only World Cup meeting of these two: France 3-1 Spain in the 2006 Round of 16 at Hanover. David Villa's early penalty had Spain dreaming of a changing of the guard; then Ribéry, Vieira and finally Zinedine Zidane — in stoppage time, in the last tournament of his career — sent the old France through and the young Spain home.

from_the_stands.question: Everyone keeps bringing up Euro 2024 like Spain own us now. But have we ever actually lost to Spain at a World Cup? It feels like the tournament that matters most is the one we never lose this fixture in.

facts: France have never lost to Spain at a World Cup. The two nations have met only once at the tournament — the 2006 Round of 16 — and France won it 3-1, Zidane scoring in stoppage time in what turned out to be the last World Cup of his career.
Spain's wins over France have all come at the European Championship: the Euro 2012 quarter-final (2-0) and the Euro 2024 semi-final (2-1), the latter on the way to Spain's European title.
France's most recent win over Spain was the 2021 Nations League final, 2-1 in Milan, decided by a late and heavily disputed Kylian Mbappé goal.
Tonight in Dallas is the first time the two have ever met in a World Cup semi-final — and only the second time they have met at a World Cup at all.
factual_brief.note: You're right about the split, and it's a real one, not a comfort. Spain have twice ended France's summers at the Euros, most recently in 2024 with a teenager's goal, and that is the meeting living rent-free in everyone's head. But the World Cup is a separate ledger, and on it France are unbeaten against Spain — one match, one win, 2006. Tonight doesn't erase Munich; it just gets contested somewhere Spain have never actually beaten you. Whether that's an omen or just trivia is the ninety minutes.
